business_problem: Peking University Library had accumulated large amounts of cataloging, visitor, and usage data, but the information was scattered across systems, making it hard for managers and service teams to use it for fine-grained operations, procurement, and reader-service decisions.
solution_summary: Peking University Library used Baidu AI Cloud's Sugar BI platform to turn fragmented library data into a unified analytics and service layer. After completing data inventory, quality normalization, integration, and data-warehouse construction, the library used Sugar BI to expose dashboards, drill-down analysis, and data-sharing services for different user groups. Management teams can see collection security, circulation, traffic, and budget signals in near real time; service departments can analyze cataloging load, supplier cycles, and document-processing performance; and readers or other university units can access tailored self-service views. The platform also supports more strategic functions such as analyzing dwell time and borrowing patterns to infer demand, then feeding those insights into acquisition decisions and service redesign. In practice, Sugar BI became the library's standard data outlet, connecting operational data, decision support, and user-facing information through one governed analytics environment.

solution_components.name: Sugar BI
solution_components.role: Provides the analytics, visualization, drill-down, and sharing environment for library data.

solution_components.name: Reader Demand Analysis System
solution_components.role: Helps the library understand reader behavior and demand through traffic and usage analytics.

solution_components.name: Literature Procurement Optimization Platform
solution_components.role: Turns circulation and subject-demand insights into more informed acquisition and cataloging decisions.

data_flow: Cataloging, visitor, and circulation data are integrated into the library's warehouse, then exposed through Sugar BI dashboards and shared data services. Managers, departments, and users query that data to analyze traffic, borrowing, supplier cycles, and subject demand, and the resulting insights flow back into procurement, staffing, and service adjustments.
business_outcome: Peking University Library gained a more data-driven operating model for circulation, acquisition, and reader-service decisions, while giving both staff and readers easier access to trusted operational information.
architecture_clues: The solution required data inventory, quality normalization, integration, and warehouse construction before dashboarding.
Different service layers were designed for management, departments, readers, and external university units instead of one generic dashboard.
Borrowing patterns and traffic signals are tied directly to acquisition planning and service redesign.
